texts: doha about how only your deeds and good name remain after you go, with a cloth sheet in it
My grandfather's old cloth sheet still hangs in the village hall where he used to sit, and when people speak of him they tell stories of his kindness, not his land; I want a doha about that

Write a doha about a person who leaves behind nothing but a plain cloth sheet and the memory of his kindness, and how people weep at his going, though he laughed when he came, because his deeds remain
cloth sheet, good name
The cloth sheet fades with the years, but the name of a good man is washed whiter by every telling
A seed planted in kindness outlives the one who sowed it, while the ash of the proud blows away and the name goes with it
After my father's cremation the ash blew off and my cousins argued over his savings, but the seed he planted by the road grew, and neighbours queued to tell how he helped them; that is what remains
doha with a seed and ash about how your good deeds are what's left of you
Please write a doha in which the ash of a dead man blows away and the seed he planted becomes a shade for strangers, to show that only one's deeds and good name remain after one is gone
seed, ash, good deeds
The yogi in our village never owned a thing, but when he died, the whole district came to his funeral, and I keep thinking about what he left behind
Kabir said live so the world laughs when you come and weeps when you go; write a doha about a yogi who lived like that, with only his deeds and name behind him
doha about a yogi whose good name stays behind when he's gone
The yogi walked softly through the world and left no footprints, only a fragrance of deeds that people still follow
yogi, name that remains
At my old teacher's funeral hundreds of former students stood in the rain with no one to make them, and I understood what a life actually leaves behind
doha about how only your deeds and good name stay after you die
Wealth is buried and houses fall, but a good deed lives in the mouths of strangers long after the doer is dust
good name remains
Write a doha in Kabir's voice saying that after death neither wealth nor beauty remains, only the deeds one did and the name one earned, so live in a way that makes the world weep at your going
My grandmother's churn is long gone but every woman in the lane still mentions how she fed everybody who came by; that is what is left of her
doha with a churn, about your deeds being what remains after death
The churn goes silent, the hands go still, but the sweetness of her giving still lives in every mouth in the lane
churn, kind deeds

Please write a doha in which a woman works her churn and shares the butter with every guest, and when she dies the whole village weeps, because the good name she earned remains when the churn is silent
doha with a mountain and a tortoise, about the name you leave when you die
Write a doha in which a mountain stands for ages and a tortoise lives for centuries, yet both are forgotten, while one good person's name is remembered for generations because of his deeds
mountain, tortoise, good name
The mountain village where my grandfather taught still tells stories about him, though the old tortoise shrine has crumbled; the people keep his name when the building is gone
The mountain endures and the tortoise lives long, but only the deeds of the good are carried on the lips of the living
The physician who healed the poor for nothing is gone, but every mended child carries a little of him still
Our village physician died last winter and for three days the shops were shut and everyone came to the lane; he left no money, but I now know what a life can leave
Please write a doha about a physician who treated the poor without fee, and whose name is spoken with love long after he is dead, because what remains of a person is only what he gave away
physician, good deeds
doha with a physician, your good deeds are what stays after you go
doha about how only your deeds and your name stay after death
When our headmaster died the school was closed for a week by the students themselves, and I realised that is what a good name is
Write a doha in Kabir's voice telling us to live in such a way that when we were born the world was glad and we cried, but when we die the world cries and we smile at what we leave
Live so that the world weeps at your going, though you came laughing into it
deeds that remain
gold, good name
Write a doha in which a man piles up gold all his life and is forgotten the day after he dies, while a poor man who gave freely is remembered by every child in the lane, since only deeds remain
My grandfather left no gold, only a reputation in the lane for never turning anyone away, and ten years after his death people still bring us sweets in his name
The gold rusts in the strongbox and is divided by quarrelling heirs, but the good name needs no keeper
doha with gold, but what remains after death is your name
gold, bell, good deeds
doha with gold and a bell, what remains is your name and deeds
The gold that the old landlord kept was spent in a year, but the bell he gave to the village school still rings and everyone calls it his bell
Please write a doha in which a bell given to the village rings long after the donor's gold has been spent and divided, to show that it is the deed and not the wealth which remains in memory
The gold scatters but the bell given in kindness still rings the donor's name across the fields
When you came, the world laughed and you cried; live now so that when you go the world cries and you are glad
After my uncle's funeral a stranger came and said he was the reason her children went to school, and my uncle had never mentioned it to us; that is what he left
Write a doha in the style of Kabir that says it is only the goodness we do that remains after we go, not our riches or our family, so we should live so that people weep at our departure
name left behind
doha about leaving a good name behind, thats all that stays
doha with a peacock, what remains after we go is our deeds

Please write a doha in which a peacock dances and wins the world's praise for a season, though its beauty is gone with it, while the quiet good deeds of an ordinary man are remembered by the village for generations
The peacock's colours leave with the peacock, but the deed of a good man is a feather that never falls
The peacock in our village yard died last year and nobody remembers its dance, but they still remember the old man who fed it every day
peacock, lasting deeds
The tongue that spoke kindly is silent now, and the fly settles where it once spoke, but the words are still alive in other mouths
Write a doha in which the tongue of a kind man is stilled by death and a fly rests where it lay, while his gentle words live on and people repeat them, since only good speech and deeds survive us
tongue, fly, good name
doha with a tongue and a fly, what stays is your name and good words
My grandfather's sweet tongue won him a reputation across three villages, and even when a fly landed on his cold face at the end, the people said he was the one man who never spoke ill
At my grandmother's funeral the queue of people she had helped without telling anyone went on for an hour, and I realised that is what is left after a life
The wealth is spent and the walls are sold, yet one kindly act still shelters strangers in its shade
Please write a doha in the manner of Kabir that says what remains of us after death is only our deeds and the name we have earned, and that the wise person lives to earn a good name, not wealth
doha about how good deeds are all that remain of us
good name, nothing else
doha about how your name is all that lasts when you go
remembered deeds
The principal of our school died and the cemetery could not hold the people who came; he never had money, but he has left a school full of former students who are teachers now
Write a doha in simple Kabir-like words that says a person is remembered only for what he gave and did, so a wise person lives rightly, so that when he dies the world weeps and he leaves smiling
Names carved on marble crumble, but a name carved in another's heart is never washed away
doha with a priest and a traveler, what remains is the name you leave
Write a doha in which a priest and a traveler are both remembered by a village, the priest for his sermons and the traveler for helping a stranger, and the verse says only what we do remains after us
A traveler once mended the roof of our village priest without asking for anything and left the next morning, and fifty years later people still tell the story
The priest is remembered for his chants, the traveler for his kindness, and the kindness outlives them both
priest, traveler, good deeds
bitter gourd, kind deeds
Write a doha in which an old woman grows a bitter gourd for the whole lane to enjoy for free, and after she dies the lane remembers her for it, since only the good one does remains
My neighbour planted a bitter gourd vine for everyone to share, and after she died the whole lane kept the vine alive in her name; this is what I call a good life
The bitter gourd on the neighbour's wall tastes of the woman who planted it, long after the woman has gone
doha with a bitter gourd, the good deeds are what remain
Walk gently on the path, for the thorn you move aside will be remembered in your name when your feet are still
My father always moved the thorn bushes off the village path, and after he died people moved on in their lives but the path remains clear, and his name is still spoken; I want a doha on that
thorn, good name
doha with a thorn, your deeds are what stay after you die
Write a doha in which a man removes a thorn from the road for the unknown travellers behind him, and when he is dead, it is that small deed that people remember instead of all the things he owned
The well that my grandfather dug for the village still serves a hundred families, and nobody remembers his home but everyone knows his name; I want a doha about it
Please write a doha about a man who digs a water well for strangers and is remembered for it long after his wealth is gone, so that the world weeps at his going, and he leaves smiling
well, lasting name
He dug a well for the thirsty and left the world, and the water still says his name to everyone who drinks
doha with a well, only the good you do stays after you die
The spinning wheel is silent, but the cloth she wove for strangers still keeps them warm, and her name is spoken with love

Write a doha in which a spinning wheel stands silent after the death of the woman who used it to make warm clothes for the poor, and her name remains with those she helped long after the wheel is broken
My grandmother's spinning wheel is in the corner and it has not been used for years, but whenever the winter comes, the old women of the village say her name, because of the shawls she made for them
doha with a spinning wheel, what stays is the name and the deeds
spinning wheel, good deeds
When you came the world laughed and you wept: live now so that when you go the world weeps and you smile
doha about living so that people miss you when you're gone
Write a doha in simple words saying that wealth and beauty and power vanish when we die, and only the good we have done and the name we have earned stay behind, so we should live accordingly
At the end of the farewell party for my retiring boss, nobody spoke about his salary or his title, only about how he treated them; I want a doha out of that
deeds that stay
doha with a philosopher's stone, only your name remains when you're gone
philosopher's stone, good name
He never found the philosopher's stone, but he turned a hundred hearts kind, and that is what the village remembers

Please write a doha in which a man spends his life seeking a philosopher's stone and is forgotten, while his neighbour who helped everyone without thinking of gain is remembered by name for generations
My uncle sought a philosopher's stone and died poor and forgotten, but the man nearby who fed strangers is still talked about in the village; I'd like a doha about that
The moon outlives the poet, but the poem outlives the moon in the hearts of those who loved it
doha with the moon, only your good name stays when you die
moon, good name
My teacher died under a full moon and the people who came that night said his deeds would be spoken of as long as the moon rises; I want a doha for him
Write a doha in which the moon looks down on the grave of a good man and the villagers still speak his name by moonlight, since the only thing that remains of us is what we did for others
Write a doha in which the fish in the pond and the grindstone at the mill outlast the man who owned them, but the village remembers him because he fed the poor from his own grain
fish, grindstone, good name
The old miller who ran the grindstone also fed the fish in the pond behind his place, and when he died the whole village came to say that this is the man who never charged the poor
The grindstone grinds for the poor and the fish swim in the pond, and the miller's name floats in the memory of both
doha with a fish and a grindstone, the good name is what stays
Write a doha in Kabir's voice telling people to do such good that when they die the world is sad and they themselves are glad, since only name and deeds are left when the body is gone
The one who lives for others dies only once, and lives for ever in a hundred mouths
My cousin's wedding was attended by a thousand people who all spoke about the kindness of his father who had died the previous year; I'd like a doha on the name that remains
deeds that remain
doha about how only deeds remain when we are gone
Please write a doha in which a sword rusts in its sheath after a warrior's death, but the people he protected still honour his name, since the only thing that lasts of any person is the good he did
doha with a sword, what remains is your name and your deeds
My grandfather's sword hangs on our wall but nobody in the family speaks of it; they speak instead of the time he stopped a riot in the village with just his words
The sword rusts and the fame of the sword rusts with it, but the deed of the defender never grows old
sword, good name
At my friend's funeral the elders could not complete the rites because so many people wanted to say a few words, and I thought how little we notice of what we leave until it is too late
doha about how only your good name remains after death
Kabir said that wealth and kin all stay behind but one's deeds echo in the world, so write a doha that tells the reader to live in such a way that the world is sad when he leaves
good name, deeds
When the body is dust, the name of a good life walks the village lanes and is welcomed everywhere
Live so the world is glad at your birth and weeps at your leaving, and you alone are smiling
doha about leaving a good name when you die
My neighbour was rude, rich and alone when he died, but the old woman across the road was mourned by two villages; I want a doha about that difference
name that outlives us
Write a doha in Kabir's voice saying what remains of anyone after death is not his money but the name he earned, so the wise live rightly and the world weeps when they are gone
My grandfather used to run his prayer beads between his fingers, but what people remember about him is the way he fed the whole street during the flood
prayer beads, good deeds
doha with prayer beads, what remains after death is the good you did
Write a doha in which a man tells his prayer beads all day and is forgotten, while his neighbour who quietly shared food during hard times is remembered by name and mourned when he is gone
The prayer beads rest in the box, but the memory of a kind hand still goes round the village
Please write a doha in which a priest reads sacred words to the crowd and is forgotten, while the poor man who helped the same crowd when they were hungry is remembered, since only deeds survive us
doha with a priest, what stays when we die is our deeds
The priest's sermon fades with the evening, but the grain given to the hungry is remembered for a lifetime
priest, good name
At the fair, people could not remember the priest's sermon from last year, but they all remember the farmer who gave free water to everyone
beggar, good name
Write a doha in which a beggar who shared his last bread is mourned by the whole street when he dies, while a rich man nearby passes unnoticed, since only deeds and name remain
doha with a beggar, what remains is the good name you leave
The old beggar at our corner died last month and the whole street collected money for his funeral, because he always shared what he got; I want a doha for him
The beggar's bowl was empty, yet his death filled the lane with weeping, for he had given more than the rich
When my aunt died I was surprised at how many people who were not in our family came to tell me what she had done for them, and I had never known; I want a doha on that
Please write a doha in the manner of Kabir about how the deeds of a person remain when his body is dust and his wealth divided, and how a good name is the only inheritance that cannot be taken
The deeds you do in the dark are the lamps people carry for you when you are gone
name left behind
doha about only your deeds mattering after you die
Write a doha in which an arrow and a thorn are forgotten by those they pierced, but a kind word is remembered for a lifetime, so what remains of a man is what he gave
arrow, thorn, good name
doha with an arrow and a thorn, only the good you do stays when you go
My uncle had a thorn in his foot and an arrow scar in his arm from his youth, but when he died, people spoke of how he never harmed anyone and always helped; I want a doha about that
The arrow and the thorn are forgotten before the wound heals, but a kindness stays in the heart till the end of days
Write a doha in which a well and a forest are the gifts of a good man to his village, and long after he is gone the water still serves and the trees still shade, carrying his name
doha with a well and a forest, what remains is the good name we leave
My great-grandfather dug a well and planted a forest for the village, and a hundred years later people still say his name when they drink or sit in the shade
He dug the well and planted the forest and went away, but every drink and every shade is his name
well, forest, good name
doha with a swan and a crossroads, the good you do stays after you die
swan, crossroads, good name
At the crossroads where he fed the swan and the stranger alike, a shrine of memory still stands though he is gone
Write a doha in which a man builds a resting place at a crossroads and feeds a swan and strangers alike, and the world weeps when he dies and remembers his name for generations
The crossroads near our lane has a bench that my grandfather put there and a swan pond he dug; he is long gone, but I hear people say his name
When the body burns, the name of a good life rises like incense, and the world weeps, but the soul smiles
Write a doha in Kabir's voice: live so that the world laughed when you were born and you cried, and the world cries when you leave and you laugh, since only name and deeds stay
The funeral of the man in our lane was crowded though he was poor, and I understood that what he left was something that cannot be counted; I would like a doha on that
doha about living so that people cry when you go
good name, remembered
Write a doha in which a rainbird calls for rain and a shroud covers a good man, and the people say that his deeds were like rain on a dry field and his name will outlast the shroud
At the funeral of our old farmer, a rainbird kept calling as they wrapped him in the shroud, and the whole village said his kindness was like rain; I want a doha on that
rainbird, shroud, good name
The rainbird cries, the shroud is white, and the good man who wears it is taken, but the rain of his kindness falls on
doha with a rainbird and a shroud, what stays is the name you leave
Write a doha in which a washerman does his work for poor families without charge and is remembered with love long after his death, since a person's true wealth is the good name he leaves behind
The washerman who cleaned clothes for the whole village for free during the epidemic is still spoken of, though he died long ago; what a person leaves is his deed
doha with a washerman, your deeds are all that remain
The washerman scrubbed the clothes of the poor and left his name clean in every household
washerman, good name
The temple's grand gift came from a rich man and is forgotten, but the water pot kept at the gate by a poor woman still holds her name
doha with a temple, only your name and deeds remain after you go
temple, good name
The big temple in our town was built by a king nobody remembers, but the old woman who gave water to pilgrims at its gate is still talked about; I want a doha for her

Please write a doha in which a man builds a grand temple for his own glory and is forgotten, while a poor woman who gave water to the weary at its gate is remembered, since only the humble deed remains
The cloud passes and the mosque stands, but only the kindness done in its courtyard is spoken of when its builder is gone
cloud, mosque, good name
My grandfather swept the courtyard of the mosque every dawn for fifty years, and when the cloud of his illness came the whole neighbourhood gathered; he left a name, not wealth
doha with a cloud and a mosque, the good name is what remains
Write a doha in which a cloud shades a mosque where a poor man swept the floor each morning, and after he dies the whole town speaks his name with love, since deeds are what remain
At the funeral of my uncle the bier was surrounded by hundreds of people, and a yogi stood quietly nearby and said, this is what a life of good deeds looks like
Write a doha in which a bier is carried by weeping villagers, and a yogi at the roadside says this is the reward of a good life, because deeds and name remain when the body is gone
doha with a bier and a yogi, what stays is our deeds
The bier is carried on a thousand shoulders while the yogi smiles, for the good man left a thousand debts of love
bier, yogi, good deeds
cleric, good name

Write a doha in which a learned cleric dies and is soon forgotten, while the simple farmer who helped the poor in secret is remembered by the whole village long after his death, because deeds are what remain
The cleric's learning is buried with the cleric, but the grain he shared with the hungry is remembered
doha with a cleric, only your name and deeds stay after you go
The cleric of our town was famous for his speeches but nobody remembers one, while everyone remembers how he once carried a sick child to the hospital on his back
Write a doha in which a person's wealth is divided and their land sold, but what stays in the village is the memory of their kindness, and the world weeps at their going
doha about how only your name stays after death
name that stays
The coin changes hands a thousand times, the land a hundred, but a good name is passed from mouth to mouth for ever
When my mother died, we sold the land, divided her few jewels, and yet everyone who met us afterwards asked about her kindness, and that is what I want a doha about
Write a doha in Kabir's manner saying that when we leave, the world remembers not our riches or rank but what we did for others, so we should live to earn a good name
deeds outlive us
When the breath of life goes out, the fragrance of good deeds still fills the room
doha about leaving a good name behind you
At the reading of my uncle's will there was nothing in it but a request to be remembered for his kindness, and in the end that is what the whole family held onto; I want a doha on that
Please write a doha in Kabir's voice telling us to live so that when we die the world weeps while we smile, because only deeds and good name remain, not riches or kin
My father died with almost nothing, yet three hundred people came to his funeral, and I cannot say what he gave them; but I know what they remember
doha about only your good name staying behind
good name stays
The wealthy man is carried out unmourned, the good man weeps in a hundred homes, and the difference is deeds
salt, net, good name
My uncle fished with a net and always gave away half the catch with salt for the poor; when he died the whole village stopped work for a day
doha with salt and a net, only your good name stays after you go
Write a doha in which a fisherman with a net shares his catch and salt with the poor all his life, and after he is dead the village remembers his kindness and speaks his name with love
The net catches and the salt preserves, but only a kind deed is kept for ever in the memory of men
At the village festival nobody remembered the rich donors from last year, but they all remembered the old man who danced with the peacock-feather crown and made the children laugh
The peacock's feather outlives the peacock, and so does the laughter of the man who gave joy to children
doha with a peacock, the good you did is what stays after you go
Write a doha in which a man who made children laugh with his peacock feather dance is remembered for generations, while the powerful are forgotten, since what remains is not rank but kindness
peacock, remembered deeds
name after death
At my friend's father's funeral, a hundred people from different villages arrived, each carrying a story of help he had given, and I realised what a rich man he was
doha about how your deeds are all that stay when you die
Write a doha in simple words saying that when a person dies, his wealth and beauty are lost, but his name and deeds remain, so he should live in a way that earns the world's tears
Dust returns to dust, but the memory of kindness has nowhere to be buried
Weep not at the departure of one who lived for others, for his name has not departed
good deeds, lasting
doha about how your good name and deeds are all that remain
Write a doha in the manner of Kabir which says that when the body goes, only deeds go on living in the world, and the wise person fills his days with kindness so that his name is blessed
When my grandmother was cremated my aunt said that she is not gone, because every person she helped will tell her story; I want a doha on this
bell, good name
The bell my grandfather placed on the village gate still rings every evening, and everyone says his name as it rings, though he died years ago; I want a doha about it
The bell rings at dusk, and in each ring the good man's name is carried to the fields
Write a doha in which a bell given by a good man long dead rings at the village gate, and the villagers say his name with love at each ring, because deeds are all that remain
doha with a bell, only your name and good deeds stay after death
